name: run-benchmark
description: Run reproducible coding-model benchmarks from a model name, CLI harness, and task list. Use when creating, executing, resuming, or verifying benchmark runs with Codex, Claudex via ccx, Claude Code, or Cursor Agent in this repository.
---

# Run Benchmark

Create one independently resumable session per task. Put the app in `benchmarks/<task>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<harness>-<model>/` (with `-2`, `-3`, and so on for repeated identical runs) and final/global evidence in `runs/<run-id>/data/`. Every invocation gets a unique `benchmark_id`; a Markdown plan generates it once and shares it across every enabled model/task run so the comparison UI can recover the exact benchmark group.

## Workflow

1. Read [references/task-catalog.md](references/task-catalog.md) for task names, application types, and seed sources.
2. Read canonical prompts locally from `<benchmark-repository>/prompts/<slug>/` (or `BENCHMARK_PROMPTS_DIR` when explicitly overridden). Select the numerically highest `v<number>.md`, including uncommitted local versions, and fail closed if the version is missing. Save the exact local file path, `https://benchmark.melvynx.dev/prompts/<slug>/<version>`, and prompt in the immutable run snapshot; do not fetch either website.
3. Confirm the requested model exists in the chosen harness when the harness exposes a model catalog. Never substitute a model silently.
4. Run:

   ```bash
   .agents/skills/run-benchmark/scripts/run-benchmark.sh \
     --model '<model-name>' \
     --harness '<codex|ccx|cc|cursor-agent>' \
     --tasks '<task-a,task-b>' \
     --effort '<level>'
   ```

   Or run a reusable Markdown plan:

   ```bash
   .agents/skills/run-benchmark/scripts/run-benchmark-plan.sh \
     benchmark-plans/<plan-name>.md
   ```

5. Inspect the printed run directory and each `verification.json`. A completed process is not proof unless the transcript is valid, a session ID was captured, and a non-empty final response was captured.
6. Run `scripts/verify-benchmark-run.sh <run-dir>...` for task-appropriate build/runtime checks, then `scripts/validate-benchmark-run.sh <run-dir>...` as the deterministic final gate.
7. Resume a task using its generated `resume-command.sh`; append new output to a new transcript file rather than overwriting the original.

## Modes

- Use `--dry-run` to create prompts, commands, metadata, ports, and app directories without calling a model.
- Use `--smoke` to ask each harness for only `HARNESS_OK`; this verifies authentication, model selection, transcript capture, and resumability without running a benchmark task.
- Use `--list-tasks` to print the catalog.
- Use `run-benchmark-plan.sh <plan.md> --dry-run` to validate and prepare every enabled plan row without calling models.

## Markdown plans

- Copy [../../../benchmark-plans/TEMPLATE.md](../../../benchmark-plans/TEMPLATE.md) to create a reusable plan.
- Set `enabled` to `yes` or `no` for each row.
- Set `tasks` to one canonical task, comma-separated tasks, or `all`.
- Add as many rows as needed to compare models and harnesses. Each row remains an independent recorded run.
- The plan runner expands rows by task and launches every model/task pair concurrently. Expect interleaved progress and one run directory per pair.

## Constraints

- Follow [.agents/rules/benchmark-runs.md](../../rules/benchmark-runs.md).
- For `ccx`, select exactly `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, or `gpt-5.6-luna`; forward effort through `--effort`.
- When a GPT model uses the Claude Code harness family, route it through `ccx`; never run a GPT model with `cc`.
- Do not combine tasks into one model session.
- Never store an app below `runs/`; `app-path.txt` and `metadata.json` must point to the task-local output directory.
- Do not mark a generated application verified until its build and real serving port have been checked.
- Every generated-task prompt requires `pnpm` exclusively when dependency installation or package scripts are needed; do not introduce npm commands or npm lockfiles.
- Keep model-facing prompts neutral: never disclose that the task is a benchmark or evaluation, never mention run evidence, and never expose a completion sentinel.
- For every non-CLI task, instruct the model to set the browser title and primary visible title to its model name using only identity information already available to it, with no additional title text.
- Every non-standalone prompt must include its allocated port as a setup, package-script, and runtime-verification requirement.
- Record each model invocation in task `metadata.json` as `model_timing.started_at`, `model_timing.completed_at`, and `model_timing.duration_ms`. Use `null` for prepared dry runs.
- Record `benchmark_id` in both `run.json` and every task `metadata.json`. Pass `--benchmark-id` only when several direct runner invocations intentionally belong to the same comparison group; otherwise let the runner generate a fresh ID.
- Analyze each valid transcript with `scripts/analyze-transcript.py`. Store a stacked progress bar and percentages for `context_gathering`, `planning`, `implementation`, and `verification` under `transcript_analysis` in task metadata. Exclude transport noise, encrypted signatures, and duplicated tool results.
- Extract the terminal harness usage record with `scripts/analyze-session-usage.py` and persist normalized input, output, cache, reasoning, total, cost, duration, turn, and raw model-usage details under `session_usage`. Use `null` only for prepared dry runs and an explicit `unavailable` object when usage cannot be recovered.
- Keep the exact raw JSONL. Redact secrets if a harness unexpectedly emits them before sharing or committing artifacts.
- Treat `prompts/<slug>/v<number>.md` as immutable after use. Add changes as a new numeric version and run `pnpm index:prompts` before committing.

# UI Skills Root

You are the routing layer for UI Skills.

This skill is shown by `npx ui-skills start` and is also available in the registry.

Use it when an agent in Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code has a clear UI goal.

If the goal is unclear, ask one short question.

If the goal is clear, choose the right category, load the smallest useful skill context, then implement.

## Protocol

1. decide if the task is UI-related
2. if not, return `no skill needed`
3. identify the likely category
4. inspect that category with the CLI
5. select the smallest useful skill set
6. load only selected skill(s)
7. implement using that context

## CLI

```bash
npx ui-skills start
npx ui-skills categories
npx ui-skills list --category <category>
npx ui-skills get <slug>
```

## Selection Rules

Prefer 1 skill.

Use 2 only when the task needs two clear angles.

Use 3 only for broad review, redesign, or multi-surface work.

Never use more than 3.

Route by topic, then stack, then specificity.

Prefer specific skills over broad skills.

Prefer framework-specific skills when the stack is obvious.

For quick cleanup, prefer the most specific craft, visual, or layout skill available.

If unsure, inspect categories and pick the safest narrow skill.

--- benchmark rules ---
# Benchmark Runs

Use these rules whenever creating, executing, resuming, or reviewing a model benchmark.

## Inputs and routing

- Require a model name, harness (`codex`, `ccx`, `cc`, or `cursor-agent`), and comma-separated task list.
- Default routing: GPT/OpenAI -> `codex` or `ccx`; Claude -> `cc`; all other models -> `cursor-agent`.
- When a GPT model is run through the Claude Code harness family, use `ccx`; reject `cc` for every `gpt*` model.
- With `ccx`, accept only `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, or `gpt-5.6-luna`, and pass `--effort` explicitly.
- Pass the model explicitly. Never silently fall back to a different model.
- Run one task per agent session so task transcripts and failures stay independent.
- Run all enabled model/task pairs concurrently. A Markdown row with two tasks produces two independent run directories.
- For reusable matrices, use `benchmark-plans/*.md`; each enabled table row creates one normal run and may select one task, a comma-separated task list, or `all`.
- Never execute rows marked `no`. Preserve the plan file unchanged as the user's reusable configuration.
- Treat this repository's `prompts/<slug>/` directory as the canonical prompt source. Read the numerically highest local `v<number>.md`, including uncommitted versions, then snapshot the exact prompt path, content, and public versioned URL into the run. Do not fetch the website or replace a missing local prompt with generic wording.

## Naming and layout

- Generate one `benchmark_id` per user-triggered benchmark operation. A plan shares that ID across every enabled model/task pair; a direct runner invocation creates a fresh ID unless its caller explicitly passes the shared `--benchmark-id`.
- Store `benchmark_id` in each run's `run.json` and every task's `metadata.json`. Keep `run_id` separate: it identifies one physical `runs/<run-id>` evidence directory, while `benchmark_id` identifies the comparison group.
- Generate run IDs as `<UTC timestamp>-<model slug>-<harness>`; append a numeric suffix on collision.
- Generate each app at `benchmarks/<task>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<harness>-<model>/`. When the same model/harness/task appears again, allocate `-2`, `-3`, and so on atomically so one benchmark group may contain repeated identical model runs without overwriting evidence.
- Write all evidence below `runs/<run-id>/data/<task>/`.
- Store no app copy under `runs/`. Store `app-path.txt`, `prompt.md`, `command.sh`, `transcript.jsonl`, `stderr.log`, `final.txt`, `session-id.txt`, `view-transcript.sh`, `resume-command.sh`, `metadata.json`, verification logs, `screenshot.png`, render metadata, and `verification.json` there.
- Do not rename individual historical result directories. Keep every task and its results below `benchmarks/<task>/`.

## Ports

- Standalone HTML tasks have no port and must open directly from an HTML file.
- Assign non-standalone GPT apps ports `9100-9199`, Claude apps `9200-9299`, and other apps `9300-9399`.
- Allocate ports atomically and skip ports already locked, listening, or recorded in `runs/`; concurrency must never produce duplicate ports.
- Add this sentence to every non-standalone app prompt: `During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port <port>, then use that port for runtime verification.`
- Add this sentence to every generated task prompt: `Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.`
- Add this sentence to every non-CLI generated task prompt: `Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.`
- Keep model-facing prompts neutral: do not mention benchmarks, evaluations, evidence storage, comparison groups, or completion sentinels.
- Record every assignment in both task metadata and the run-level `ports.json` index.

## Timing

- Measure each task's harness invocation from immediately before harness execution until it returns, including failed invocations.
- Record UTC `started_at`, UTC `completed_at`, and integer `duration_ms` under `model_timing` in the task's `metadata.json`.
- Set `model_timing` to `null` for prepared dry runs; do not invent an elapsed time when no model ran.

## Transcript phases

- Analyze substantive model-authored transcript activity after each run and record it under `transcript_analysis` in task `metadata.json`.
